assumptions: ENA's feature and qualifier tables are those its own validator reads, as cached.
limits: Builds the files; Webin-CLI's own validation and the upload are not run here.
bio.jane/contract.question: What flat file and manifest does ENA's Webin-CLI take for this record, and what would its validator refuse?

description: Turn a record into what ENA's Webin-CLI takes for an annotated sequence (`-context sequence`): an ENA flat file (`.embl`) and its manifest. Features are checked against the tables ENA's own validator reads, so what Webin-CLI would refuse (an unknown key, a missing mandatory qualifier, a double quote in a value, a duplicate feature) is refused or rewritten here, by name. A description under 10 characters, an entry under 100 bp and a missing study are reported first. It WRITES FILES and sends nothing.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

collection_date.description: when the sample was collected, on the source feature. Optional, but must be INSDC-legal; a construct takes a missing-value term such as `missing: lab stock`.

description.description: the DE line, what the sequence is. Left empty, each record's own DEFINITION is used; ENA refuses one shorter than 10 characters.

genbank.description: the record to submit, as GenBank text. Its features, topology and DEFINITION are read from it.

geo_loc_name.description: where the sample came from, from the INSDC vocabulary, or a missing-value term.

mol_type.description: the source feature's mandatory /mol_type. `other DNA` is the INSDC value for a synthetic construct.

organism.description: the scientific name of the source organism; ENA checks it against its taxonomy. `synthetic construct` is a real answer for a built vector.

study.description: the Webin Portal study accession (PRJEB… or ERP…). Webin-CLI refuses a set without one; left empty, the files are written and the reason reported.

topology.description: circular for a plasmid (the ID line; only then may a feature cross the origin). Left empty, the record's own topology is used. Values:  (From the record), circular (Circular), linear (Linear). Advanced.

name: build_ena_submission

changes.description: every feature the writer refused, rewrote or left a qualifier off, each with ENA's reason

command.description: the exact gzip and webin-cli invocation, with -validate

files.description: the flat file and its manifest, each with its `name` and `text`. Gzip the flat file before running Webin-CLI; the manifest already names the `.gz`

flatFile.description: the `.embl` alone, for reading or diffing

problems.description: why Webin-CLI will refuse the set as it stands: a short description, a short entry, no study, or a malformed date or locality. Empty means none of those, never that the validator will be silent

reading.description: what the set is, generated from what was written
